name: Lateral Femoral Cutaneous Neuropathy - Iatrogenic/Postsurgical
definition: Injury of the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve after pelvic, hip or abdominal procedures, producing anterolateral thigh sensory pain without motor deficit.

investigations.principle: Diagnosis is mainly clinical; electrodiagnostics or ultrasound are selective.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, labral, tendon, ligament, infection, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Persistent focal neuroma/entrapment symptoms may require specialist intervention.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

patientEducation.summary: Injury of the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve after pelvic, hip or abdominal procedures, producing anterolateral thigh sensory pain without motor deficit.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, rapidly progressive weakness, suspected serious infection, airway/vascular symptoms, unreduced dislocation or other listed red flags.
